    τῇ πίστει, μὴ ἐργαζόμενοι τὰ ἔργα τῆς πίστεως. 2. πολλοὶ οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν μετενόησαν, καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ κατοίκησις
    αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ πύργῳ. 3. ἕτεροι δὲ εἰς τέλος μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συζῶντες καὶ φθειρόμενοι ταῖς κενοδοξίαις
    τῶν ἐθνῶν ἀπέστησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἔπραξαν τὰς πράξεις τῶν ἐθνῶν. οὗτοι μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐλογίσθησαν.

    ἐστίν· ἀλλ᾿ ἡ μετάνοια αὐτῶν ταχινὴ ὀφείλει εἶναι, ἵνα ἡ κατοικία αὐτῶν γένηται ἐντὸς τοῦ πύργου·

translation:
  text: '“Those who handed in rods that were two-thirds dry and one-third green are people who had been
    faithful, but became wealthy and honored among the nations. They clothed themselves in great arrogance
    and became proud. They abandoned the truth and did not keep company with the righteous, but lived
    as the nations do. This way became more pleasant to them. Yet they did not turn away from God; they
    remained in the faith without doing the works of faith.”[a]


    2. “Many of them repented, and their dwelling came to be in the tower.”


    3. “Others, however, kept living with the nations to the end, were corrupted by the nations’ empty
    glories, turned away from God and did the nations’ deeds. These were counted with the nations.”[b]


    4. “Others among them wavered, having no hope of being saved because of the deeds they had done. Others
    wavered and made divisions among themselves. For these, and for those who wavered because of their
    deeds, there is still an opportunity to repent.[c] But their repentance must be quick, so that their
    dwelling may be inside the tower. Death is near to those who do not repent but persist in their pleasures.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Nations” renders ethne in the vision’s contrast between the righteous community and its surroundings.
      The draft retains both their continued faith and their failure to do its works; it does not erase
      either statement. The rod is explicitly two-thirds dry, one-third green.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Corrupted” follows Athos and the working Greek. Michigan’s published transcription has a form
      meaning “carried away,” with damaged letters nearby. Alternative: “Others kept living with the nations
      to the end, were carried away by the nations’ empty glories, turned away from God and did the nations’
      deeds.” This semantic difference remains visible without a new source substitution here.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The bounded POB selection adds kai, “and,” partly preserved in Michigan, Bonner printed p.
      111, papyrus p. 51 line 32: the alpha is restored, while kappa and iota are printed outside brackets.
      Reported Latin parallels also distinguish both groups. Athos lacks the conjunction. Shorter alternative:
      “For those who wavered because of their deeds, there is still an opportunity to repent.” The draft
      includes both the division-making group and those despairing because of deeds; the requirement of
      quick repentance and warning of death remain.'
lexical_decisions:
- source_word: μετάνοια / διψυχεῖν
  chosen: repentance / waver
  alternatives:
  - turning back / be double-minded
  rationale: Keep the concrete change of deeds, conditions and warnings. Do not erase the difference between
    an opportunity to repent and its actual acceptance.
- source_word: καὶ τοῖς διψυχήσασι
  chosen: and for those who wavered
  alternatives:
  - for those who wavered (shorter Athos)
  rationale: Partly preserved Michigan conjunction broadens the offer to both named groups; its restored
    alpha and the response condition are explicit.
